title: WPMS/13499/1995 of ARUN KUMAR AGARWAL Vs A.D.J. and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.4645 of 2001 (M/S)
(Old No.13499 of 1995)
Arun Kumar Agarwal and others. .......Petitioners

Versus
Additional District Judge, Haridwar and others.
.......Respondents
Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner nos.1 to 6 and Mr. Nagesh
Agarwal, Advocate for the petitioner no.7.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State/respondent
nos.1 & 2.
Mr. S.K. Jain, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. B.S. Thind, Advocate for the
respondent nos.4 to 8 & 11 to 14.
Dated: December 27, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Present petition has been filed by the petitioners
for quashing the judgment and order-dated 05.05.1995
passed by the IInd Additional District Judge, Haridwar,
in Small Cause Revision No.2 of 1991 "Smt. Kamlesh
Rani Vs. Smt. Dayawati and others", by which the
revision filed by the legal heirs of the landlord has been
allowed and the judgment of Small Causes Court/Civil
Judge, Roorkee dated 04.02.1991 has been set aside
and the petitioners has been directed to handover the
vacant possession of the accommodation in dispute to
the respondents within 30 days.
2. Facts giving rise to the present petition are that
on 18.09.1972, Shri Om Prakash Jain served a notice
upon Shri Vishwa Mittar Agarwal. In the notice, it was
asserted that as per the new U.P. (Urban Building)
Regulation of Letting Rent and Eviction Act, 1972
(hereinafter referred to as the "Act"), Shri Om Prakash

2
Jain was entitled for increase of rent and payment of
tax by the tenant. An arrear of ` 799.14 was also
claimed. It was also asserted that Shri Vishwa Mittar
Agarwal had sublet the first floor of the house to his
brother Shri Aryamitra Agarwal without permission
and consent of Shri Om Prakash Jain. It was alleged
that the house was given for residential purposes, but
without any prior permission, the premises was being
used for bakery business and a bhatti had been
erected which decreased the value of the property. Shri
Vishwa Mittar Agarwal replied the said notice and
denied that Shri Aryamitra Agarwal was living as sikmi
tenant, as he had been living from 1946 and there was
no case of subletting. It was also replied that the bhatti
was in the accommodation from the very beginning and
earlier, it was being used for the business of Hair Oil,
Soap etc. and is not being used for bakery business. No
new bhatti has been set up and the existence and use
of bhatti is within the full knowledge of the landlords
since very longtime. Demand for payment of enhanced
rent and tax was denied. On 21.04.1973, another
notice was served to Aryamitra Agarwal. The
allegations were denied and the amount of rent
demand, as arrears, were sent by cheque under
protest. Thereafter, on 21.05.1975, the plaintiff/
landlord Shri Om Prakash Jain filed S.C.C. Suit No.30
of 1975 for ejectment against the defendant no.1 Shri
Vishwa Mittar Agarwal (tenant) and Shri Aryamitra
Agarwal (subtenant) in the Court of Small Causes,
Roorkee, Saharanpur. They died during the pendency
of litigation and their heirs were substituted. After the

3
pleadings were exchanged, both the parties led their
oral and documentary evidence. After evaluating
evidence on record, the Judge, Small Causes Court/
Civil Judge, Roorkee on 04.02.1991 dismissed the
S.C.C. Suit No.30 of 1975 by observing in the order
that there was a Hindu Undivided Family and Shri
Aryamitra Agarwal had been living in the
accommodation since 1948. The plaintiffs had made no
objection to his living and after enforcement of the Act,
the benefit of Section 14 accrued. The breaking of the
Joint Hindu Family Business would not destroy the
right of Shri Aryamitra Agarwal to stay in the
accommodation. As regards the bakery business and
the bhatti, the finding recorded is that they are old
businesses and the plaintiffs had never objected to the
same. It would also be deemed that they had waived
their rights to object and had also acquiesced and after
a lapse of considerable time, no objection could be
raised. Against the judgment and order dated
04.02.1991 passed by the Judge, Small Causes Court/
Civil Judge, Roorkee, the legal heirs of the landlord
Shri Om Prakash Jain filed S.C.C. Revision No.2 of
1991 before the District Judge, Haridwar. The IInd
Additional District Judge, Haridwar, vide judgment and
order dated 05.05.1995, allowed the said revision and
set aside the judgment and order dated 04.02.1991
and decreed the suit of the plaintiffs. Aggrieved by the
judgment and decree dated 05.05.1995 passed by the
IInd Additional District Judge, Haridwar, in S.C.C.
Revision No.2 of 1991 "Smt. Kamlesh Rani Vs. Smt.
Dayawati and others", present petition has been filed.

4
3. Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate and Mr.
Nagesh Agarwal appearing for the petitioners
submitted that the Revisional Court committed legal
error by distinguishing A.L. J. 1982 page 916, as Shri
Om Prakash had given a notice in 1972 and 1973 but
had not acted upon the same by instituting suit. On
the very same facts, he gave fresh notice in May, 1975
and thereafter, instituted the suit under Section 20 of
the "Act" and thus, this action of Shri Om Prakash
Jain will clearly amount to approve and condoning the
possession of Shri Aryamitra in accommodation in
dispute. They submitted that from the evidence on
record, it is established that Shri Aryamitra Agarwal
was living since 1948 and admittedly, Shri Om Prakash
Jain had never objected to his possession for very long
period, it would be assumed that the benefit of Section
14 of the Act would accrue to Shri Aryamitra Agarwal
and no finding of subletting can be recorded and in any
case, the Revisional Court had not at all recorded
finding that Shri Aryamitra Agarwal was paying any
rent to Shri Vishwamitra Agarwal and therefore, the
residents of Shri Aryamitra Agarwal with his brother
Shri Vishwamitra Agarwal cannot amount to status of
sikmi tenant or subletting. In the instant case, there is
no assertion accepting any rent by Shri Vishwamitra
from Shri Aryamitra Agarwal either in the plaint or
replica or in the oral statement on behalf of the
plaintiff. They argued that the Revisional Court has
erroneously ignored the income assessment orders,
which clearly record the existence of Hindu Undivided
Family amongst brothers of Musaddi Lal and in fact,

5
the income tax assessment orders for the year of
ending 31.03.1950 and 31.03.1952 has been totally
ignored and this amount to a patent error of law
apparent on the face of record. They further submitted
that so far as the documents of information relating to
the birth of son of Aryamitra is concerned, the finding
of the Revisional Court does not pertain to the
accommodation in question, same is wholly incorrect,
as the Mohalla, which has been mentioned as Purani
Kotwali, is the same as Mohalla Rajputan East. The
Revisional Court ignored the material evidence and has
recorded perverse finding that the bhatti was
constructed for bakery business without the consent of
the landlord and was the inconsistent user, as evidence
on record established that the bhatti existed since
1948 and was being used for different business by the
petitioners from time to time and in fact, 1953 family
arrangement clearly records the existence of the
business on the ground floor admittedly, there is no
evidence showing that before 1972, Shri Om Prakash
Jain had at any time objected to the existence of the
bhatti and carrying on the business of the ground floor
of the accommodation. In fact, despite of the full
knowledge of the existence of business, the rent was
accepted by Shri Om Prakash Jain. They contended
that the landlords are living elsewhere and they do not
require the accommodation themselves. It is also
submitted that the property has been sold to Shri
Pradeep Kumar Saini and three others on 04.10.2006
and they have become the owner on the same day.
Learned counsel for the petitioners argued that the

6
Revisional Court has failed to appreciate material
evidence on record, namely, voter list, assessment
house and water tax and the family arrangement of
1953, which clearly shows that Shri Aryamitra Agarwal
was living on the upper story of the accommodation
since 1948 and that being so, it cannot be held that his
residence was that of a sikmi tenant. Learned counsel
for the petitioners submitted that the Court below has
overlooked the oral evidence of record, which
establishes that Shri Aryamitra Agarwal has been
residing in the accommodation since beginning i.e.
1948. In fact, the notice was given by Shri Om Prakash
Jain in 1972 and that itself shows that Shri Aryamitra
Agarwal was living in the accommodation from much
earlier. In support of their submission, learned counsel
for the petitioners relied upon the judgments reported
in 1982 ALJ 916 "Smt. Shyam Kumari Gupta Vs.
Shankar Sahai and another, Allahabad Rent Cases
1991 page 93 "Badri Nath Garg Vs. Sheo Tandon", AIR
1966 Allahabad 214 "Mahabir Singh Vs. Anant Ram
and others", ARC 1980 page 589 "Tikka Manujendra
Shah Vs. IIIrd Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Saharanpur and others" and submitted that the
judgment passed by the Revisional Court is not
sustainable in the eyes of law, therefore, judgment and
order dated 05.05.1995 passed by the IInd Additional
District Judge, Haridwar be quashed.
4. Mr. S.K. Jain, Senior Advocate for the respondent
nos.4 to 8 & 11 to 14 submitted that the present writ
petition has been filed by the legal heirs of the tenant

7
Vishwa Mittar Agarwal and not by the legal heirs of the
sub-tenants Arya Mittar, who are respondent nos.9 &
10. By not contesting the present writ petition, they
have admitted that they are residing in the whole
house in question as a sub-tenant. He submitted that
the defendants failed to prove that there was any joint
Hindu Family amongst the Musaddi Lal as his three
sons. It was neither disclosed by any of the defendants
that who was the karta of the Joint Hindu Family nor
filed any documents to show this fact. He submitted
that the defendants failed to prove that the disputed
house was in the tenancy of Joint Hindu Family and
Arya Mittar resides as brother of Vishwa Mittar in the
house in question from 1948 to 1972. He submitted
that the defendant no.1 also failed to prove that Vishwa
Mittar resided in the house in question from 1972. In
the written statement of defendant no.1, he admitted
that Vishwa Mittar is the exclusive tenant of the house
in question since 1969 and in the written statement of
2/1, he admitted that from very beginning, the rent
was being paid through Shri Vishwa Mittar Agarwal the
defendant no.1. The defendant no.2/1 also stated that
the possession of defendant no.2 Arya Mittar ever
remained as that of a tenants and after the death of
Shri Musaddi Lal, all his tenancy rights also devolved
upon all the three brothers. He submitted that in these
circumstances, the possession of defendant no.2
remained as that of a co-tenant. He submitted that it is
not a case of the defendants that the house in question
was let out to defendant no.1 as a karta of Joint Hindu
Family. The documents filed by the defendants are

8
regarding the tenancy of shop, which is a different
property and not disputed in the said case. Learned
Senior Advocate for the respondent then submitted
that the simple case of the plaint is that the defendant
no.1 Vishwa Mittar was the sole tenant in the house in
question who sublet to his brother defendant no.2 Arya
Mittar in 1973, same is confirmed by documents also
in 1975. He submitted that in the W.S. of defendant
no.1, he admitted that the shop was let out in 1925-26,
but he has falsely stated that the shop situated in the
north of the disputed house (Hawali) is the part of
Hawali, but it is proved by the evidence on record that
both are quite independent separate property.
According to learned counsel for the respondent the
period of tenancy is divided into three parts i.e. 1948 to
1969, 1969 to 1973 and 1973 till filing of the suit and
thereafter. He submitted that there is no iota of
evidence on the record regarding that Arya Mittra was
residing in the house from 1948 to 1973. There is also
no iota of evidence on the record regarding the fact that
Vishwa Mittar is residing in the house in question from
1973 till filing of the suit and thereafter. He submitted
that there is categorical finding of the Revisional Court
that the defendant no.2 Arya Mittar never resided in
the house in question with the consent of the landlord.
There is also categorical finding of the Revisional Court
that the disputed house in question was let out in
1948 to defendant no.1 and he sublet it to the
defendant no.2 without the permission in writing of the
landlord and without the permission of the landlord,
the defendant no.1 had changed the use of the house

9
in question from residential into commercial. Learned
Senior Advocate lastly submitted that the finding of the
Revisional Court, regarding the sub tenancy as well as
change of the use of the property from residential into
commercial, are based on the material on record and
there is no perversity and illegality in the finding of the
Revisional Court. In support of his submission, learned
Senior Advocate relied upon the judgments reported in
2002 SCC (9) page 499 C, 2000 ALR (38) page 319
(S.C.), 2011 ARC Vol.1 page 697, 1998 ALR (33) page
612, 2005 SCC (1) page 31, 2004 SCC (3) page 682.
5. I have considered the submission advanced by the
learned counsel for the parties and have perused the
papers available on record.
6. Both the parties do not dispute that at the time of
giving on rent, no rent was fixed for the property in
dispute. It is also not disputed that one shop at
northern side of the disputed property was let out to
the petitioners in the year 1925-26 and that shop is
not in dispute.
7. Respondent landlord came up with the case that
disputed property was given on rent to defendant no.1
Late Vishwa Mittra, but he without permission of the
landlord sublet the same to his brother Late Aryamitra.
This was denied by the petitioners and it was said that
Late Mussaddi Lal and his sons, namely, Vishwa
Mittra, Aryamitra and Devmitra were living together as
Joint Hindu Family. Their family business was being

10
done in the name of Firm Mussaddi Lal Arya Mittra. In
the year 1953, Mussaddi Lal and Arya Mittra came out
of the Firm Mussaddi Lal Arya Mittra, and defendant
no.1 Vishwamitra and Devmitra were partners on the
Firm Mussaddi Lal Arya Mittra. Defendant, in his
written statement, also stated that in the year 1969
dispute arose between defendant no.1 and Devmitra,
and Firm was dissolved. Thus, disputed property came
into the share of defendant no.1. He constructed the
Bhatti and opened Bakery business. He denied that
defendant no.2 is sub-tenant. It is also stated by the
defendant no.1 that rent receipts of the shop and
house were given in the name of Mussaddi Lal Arya
Mittra. In his statement, D.W.1 stated that landlord
used to give receipt and he had receipts for 15-20
years. But he neither filed the same in the Court nor
disclosed any reason for not filing the rent receipts. By
filing the receipts, he could have proved that disputed
property was given on rent to Joint Hindu Family. The
stand of the plaintiff/landlord was that accommodation
was given on oral rent. One Baleshwar Kumar Jain was
examined as P.W.1. In his statement, he stated that
the disputed accommodation was always used for
residential purpose and Aryamitra was kept as sub-tenant. D.W.1 Vishwamitra, in his cross-examination,
stated that the shop Golden Bakery in which he is
doing business was joint business till 1953 but
thereafter; he alone does business in that shop. After
1969, he alone is tenant of the shop. On the basis of
this statement, the learned Lower Revisional Court
held that Vishwamitra was doing his business alone in

11
the shop since 1953 and after 1969, he alone is a
tenant of the shop and he had no connection with
Aryamitra, Devmitra and their legal heirs. Learned
Lower Revisional Court on the basis of oral evidence
further held that disputed property was in the tenancy
of defendant no.1 Vishwamitra. The learned Revisional
Court reached to the conclusion that defendant no.1,
without consent of the landlord, kept defendant no.2 as
sub-tenant and property was in inconsistent use. The
case law cited by the learned counsel for the petitioners
on this point does not help him in view of the fact that
plaintiff served notice in the year 1972 and 1973 and
thereafter, instituted the suit in the year 1975. There is
nothing on record, which could show that any such
consent was ever given by the landlord. Moreover, it
was not the case of the defendants that the house in
question was let out to defendant no.1 as a Karta of
Joint Hindu Family. The learned Lower Revisional
Court also held that disputed property was given for
residential use, but the defendant, by installing bakery
Bhatti, changed the use. For reaching this conclusion,
the learned Revisional Court relied the statement of
Dev Dutt and Baleshwar Kumar Jain. The finding of
the Revisional Court regarding sub-tenancy as well as
the change of use of the property in question is based
on the material on record and cannot be interfered in
the writ petition.
8. In view of above discussion, I do not find any
perversity or illegality in the judgment of the learned
Lower Revisional Court. Consequently, the writ petition

12
is dismissed. Considering the fact that matter is
pending for last more than 28 years, the petitioners are
given time upto 31st August, 2014 to vacate the
premises in dispute.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 27.12.2013
